title: Delegated service-account creation UI + approval workflow with RBAC v2 entitlements
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Currently service accounts are predominantly created by platform engineers or via back-end provisioning flows which makes it hard for product teams to self-serve while preserving least-privilege, ownership, and audit fidelity. We need a delegated creation path in the Admin Console that enforces RBAC v2 entitlements, ties creation to SSO groups for approvers, attaches a template-driven least-privilege role, and emits structured audit events for SIEM ingestion.

Goals:
- Allow scoped, auditable creation of service accounts from the Console by authorized non-admins (team leads, infra owners) with an approval flow.
- Enforce RBAC v2 rules: creator must have 'sa:create' permission on target project namespace; approver must be mapped from SSO group -> entitlement.
- Attach a named least-privilege template at creation time; enforce owners and TTL/expiration if requested.
- Create structured audit logs (JSON) for creation/approval/rotation/deletion with correlation_id to trace in ELK/Splunk.
- Provide an API equivalent (admin endpoints) for terraform/infra-as-code adoption.

Key requirements / constraints:
1) UI form with fields: name, namespace/project, template (dropdown), owner (user or SSO group), expiration (optional), justification (text), requested-scopes (read-only summary based on template).
2) Approval workflow: immediate approval if creator is in approver group for that namespace OR create a pending request that notifies approvers via email/Slack and requires explicit 'Approve' action.
3) Default templates: project-level defaults, plus override templates for internal tooling (cronjobs, data pipelines). Templates are versioned and immutable once published.
4) Audit schema must include: event_type, actor, target_resource, template_id, requested_scopes, decision, approver, correlation_id, timestamp, request_id. Logs ship to the central audit pipeline and marked with retention class.
5) Service account secrets: support issuing short-lived ephemeral tokens (OIDC/STS style) and long-lived keys only when justified + auto-rotation schedule. Keys must be opaque and recorded in audit.
6) RBAC v2 mapping: implement a pre-check endpoint that evaluates "can_create_sa(actor, namespace, template)" returning reason codes for failures to drive UI messaging.
7) Migration: provide a migration path for existing SAs created via old flow (tagging owners, retro-applying templates where possible, and emitting a migration-audit event).

Non-goals: implementing the full token rotation service (separate ticket), reworking the entire RBAC engine (we'll call the new evaluation API), and building a new notification system (we'll reuse notifications service).

Acceptance criteria:
- Console: create-SA flow available behind feature flag 'delegated_sa_ui' with RBAC checks and approval flow.
- API parity: POST /admin/service-accounts/request and /admin/service-accounts/approve endpoints implemented with OpenAPI spec and tests.
- Structured audit events emitted for request, approve, reject, create, key_issue, key_rotate, and delete.
- E2E test: developer user in example SSO group requests SA, approver approves, SA is created with template applied, audit shows full event chain and correlation_id.
- UX copy reviewed and signed off by Design and PM.

Related documents / artefacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Delegated+Service+Account+Design (design spec + wireframes)
- GitHub epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/labels/sa-delegation-epic
- PR prototype (UI): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1248
- Existing RBAC v2 evaluator: internal endpoint /api/v2/rbac/evaluate (see ENG-41272 for context)

Rollout plan:
Phase 1 (canary): enable feature flag for 10 internal teams, monitor audit events, approver latency, SA creation failures.
Phase 2: enable for all internal orgs and selected pilot customers with dedicated support.
Phase 3: GA and enable Terraform provider support.

Metrics to monitor: number of delegated requests, approval latency (median), percent auto-approved, SA creation errors, proportion of SAs with expiration set, audit log delivery success rate.

Security notes: Security review required (SSO entitlement mappings, audit retention, key issuance policy). Long-lived keys must require 2-factor approval from an admin group.
